subject: History
chapter: Kings, Farmers and Towns: Early States and Economies
central_question: How do inscriptions, texts, coins and archaeology help historians explain the growth of early states, agrarian change, towns and trade from c. 600 BCE to 600 CE?
in_scope_units: Prinsep, Piyadassi and the development of epigraphy.
The sixteen mahajanapadas and the growth of Magadha.
The Mauryan Empire, its sources, administration and limits.
Post-Mauryan chiefs, kings, divine claims, samantas and prashastis.
Popular perceptions of rulers and changing agricultural production.
Rural differentiation, land grants and new elites.
New cities, urban populations, crafts and guilds.
Historical use and limitations of inscriptional evidence.
banned_topics: Detailed Harappan urbanism, treated in the previous chapter.
Detailed kinship, caste and Mahabharata social history, treated in the next chapter.

known_pitfalls.correction: Some were ruled by kings, while ganas or sanghas shared power among several rajas.

known_pitfalls.claim: The Mauryan Empire had one uniform administrative system in every region.
known_pitfalls.correction: Its diverse geography and great extent make uniform control unlikely; control was probably strongest near major centres.
They are praise compositions that project patrons' idealised power and must be checked against other evidence.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Exercise 5 on the problems of epigraphy.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with questions 1-5 in the 100-150 word section, essay questions 6-9, Map work 10 and Projects 11-12.
